questions.stem: A 49-year-old librarian attends the emergency department with a painful swollen right fist. She had sustained a bite injury from a stray cat 24 hours before. On examination her temperature is 38.1°C. There is an incisional wound with purulent cellulitis over the MCP joint of the ring finger on the right hand. Movement in the joint is very painful and limited. There is tracking erythema spreading up toward her elbow. Blood cultures are taken, and she is taken to theatre by the plastic surgeons for exploration and debridement of the wound. Investigations: Blood cultures Day 1: small gram-negative coccobacilli Day 2: grey mucous colonies on blood agar at 37°C. No growth on MacConkey agar
questions.lead_in: What antibiotic would be active against this organism?
questions.explanation: Penicillin The organism is most likely to be Pasteurella multocida, given the history of a penetrating cat bite, the aggressive nature of the infection manifest in the speed of onset, the associated bacteremia, and the likely tenosynovitis. The microbiology findings are consistent with this epidemiologic and clinical suspicion. Penicillin sensitivity is used within the laboratory to distinguish Pasteurella species from other gram-negative bacilli.
questions.source: Comprehensive Review of ID · Quiz 8 Q36

questions.stem: A patient presents to the emergency department with a painful left hand after being bitten by a cat. He has a deep puncture wound with some purulent drainage and surrounding cellulitis. Wound cultures are taken, and he is given broad-spectrum antibiotics and tetanus vaccination.
questions.lead_in: What bacterium is the most likely cause of his infection?
questions.explanation: Pasteurella multocida Gram-negative anaerobes, including Pasteurella, are commonly associated with both cat and dog bites.
questions.source: Comprehensive Review of ID · Quiz 9 Q31

questions.question: Farmer with a lesion on his finger after being bitten by a sheep

cohort_answer.text: Orf (caused by Parapoxvirus) - found in sheep/goats/cattle/deer, occupational exposure, incubation 3-5 days, self-limiting, no tx needed, may trial topical cidofovir or imiquimod

questions.question: [image-based question: Staph streak on BAP shown with satelliting colonies]

parts.text: Name 3 genera of bacteria that have this characteristic.

questions.model_answer: Three genera exhibiting satellite phenomenon around a Staphylococcus streak on blood agar (due to Staph-produced NAD/hemin/X-V factors): (1) Haemophilus (e.g. H. influenzae, requires X and V factors). (2) Aggregatibacter (formerly Actinobacillus) actinomycetemcomitans. (3) Granulicatella / Abiotrophia (nutritionally variant streptococci, satellite due to pyridoxal requirement).

questions.question: 24-year old with left neck fluctuant mass. It is warm, and erythematous and the patient is febrile. Name the pathogen and the MOST APPROPRIATE sample and method of diagnosis.

parts.text: Variant: He was bit in the neck by a rabbit
Variant: He just immigrated from the Phillipines and also describes weight loss.
Variant: He ate steak tartare 1 week prior
Variant: He has a sore throat with exudate

questions.model_answer: Base case (fluctuant, warm, erythematous neck mass, febrile - acute suppurative lymphadenitis): pathogen Staphylococcus aureus (or Streptococcus pyogenes); sample/method - needle aspiration of the fluctuant node for Gram stain and culture. a) Rabbit bite variant: Francisella tularensis (tularemia) - or Pasteurella multocida; sample/method - lymph node aspirate/biopsy for culture (notify lab given F. tularensis biosafety risk) and/or serology (acute and convalescent tularemia serology). b) Philippines immigrant with weight loss variant: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (scrofula/TB lymphadenitis); sample/method - fine-needle aspiration or excisional lymph node biopsy for AFB smear, mycobacterial culture, and NAAT (Xpert MTB/RIF). c) Steak tartare variant: Toxoplasma gondii (toxoplasmic lymphadenitis from undercooked meat); sample/method - serology (Toxoplasma IgM/IgG), as histology alone is nonspecific and organism isolation from lymph node is not typically performed. d) Sore throat with exudate variant: Group A Streptococcus (Streptococcus pyogenes) - or Epstein-Barr virus if mononucleosis suspected; sample/method - throat swab for rapid antigen/culture (or heterophile antibody/Monospot test if EBV suspected).
